engagement_background.objective: Cascade Services engaged Treya Partners to achieve $0.87–$1.7 million in annual procurement savings (creating roughly $16.6 million in enterprise value), leverage its enterprise-wide buying power, and stand-up a best-in-class, repeatable procurement process within a 5- to 6-month window.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Nine spend categories with a $32.9 million baseline (≈$26.5 million addressable) are in scope: HVACR OEM/Distributors, HVACR & Plumbing Supplies, Advertising, General Industrial/Electrical Supplies, Electronic Payment Processing, Telecom – Data & Voice, Fleet, Uniforms, and Commercial Print. Low-spend or low-opportunity categories may be dropped or recategorized during the project; direct field service labor and any parallel sourcing efforts by Cascade are excluded.
constraints_challenges: Decentralized, multi-branch purchasing limits current leverage and complicates change management.
Supplier data requests may face slow or non-responsive vendors, creating baseline and analysis gaps.
Stakeholder availability and willingness to participate (data provision, reviews, negotiations) is critical and may be limited.
Incumbent supplier sensitivities and the risk of informal ‘side conversations’ could undermine unified negotiation strategy.
Aggressive timeline – savings to be implemented by late September 2025 to meet private-equity value-creation targets.
Internal systems hold only summary AP data; detailed line-item usage often must be sourced from suppliers, leading to potential data quality issues.

procurement_environment.data_availability: Company provided AP data for Jan–Dec 2024; limited internal line-item usage or contract repository exists, so supplier-provided data is required for most categories.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Spend data resides in AP files with varied vendor naming; historical usage data is incomplete and dependent on supplier cooperation, leading to potential baseline gaps.
